title: Strip Unicode format characters from logged page text
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Obsidian syntax such as `%%`, `==`, and `#tag` also passes. This pre-dates the overnight work (M1). Strip or replace Unicode category Cf in row text (titles and any presentation text), keeping the hex marker payload byte-exact. Also decide whether to neutralize `%%` comments and `#` tags in titles.

Cover both paths, ideally with one shared sanitizer used by the log row writer and the artifact renderer, so they cannot drift (they already differ: index escapes `!`, capture does not). The regression test should feed a hostile title through both the daily log and a regenerated artifact file.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test reproducing the reported gap fails before the fix and passes after; the full Rust and extension suites are green. If the test shows the finding is wrong, close as not reproduced with the reason.

(2) New request forget_adopted_contracts { expected_revision } (the state revision from (1)). Under the config lock the host rereads the file; if the revision still matches it renames it aside to adopted-contracts.json.<timestamp>.bak (the backup_invalid pattern for config.toml), then records the current contracts as a fresh file; a mismatch is conflict. Reply config_result. Update the refusal text (config::ADOPTED_CONTRACTS_REPAIR) to point at the button.

title: Service: keep a run's key until its terminal status is durable
description: Codex review of PR #75 (P2): Inner::finish in host/src/service/supervisor.rs frees the run's scheduler slot and key and drops its control even when the terminal write_status fails (disk full, permissions, transient I/O). The record then still says queued or running, get_run reports it active until a service restart, and another run for the same record key can start. Design choice needed: holding the slot until the write succeeds can strand the queue on a persistently failing disk, so prefer bounded retries plus an in-memory terminal state that get_run/list_runs report, keep the key reserved until the state is durable or the service restarts, and let recovery settle the record.
acceptance_criteria: A failing terminal status write never lets a second run start for the same record key, get_run reports the true end state, a later successful write or restart recovery makes the record durable, the queue is never stranded, fault-injection tests pin each case, and the full gate in the plan's Global Constraints is green.

close_reason: Shipped in the service-hardening PR: bounded terminal-write retries, in-memory end state, key kept reserved until durable.

title: Replace the hand-written SQLite snapshot with an incremental real-SQLite index
description: Step 6.6 (host/src/index.rs) emits index.db with a custom SQLite file-format writer (build_sqlite) and keeps the real cache in index-state.json. Every publish re-derives all artifacts from the full event history, serializes the whole-history JSON state (64 MiB cap, after which index updates fail), and rewrites the entire index.db. Both are whole-file atomic replacements, so concurrent host processes are last-writer-wins. The writer supports no secondary indexes or overflow records, so M3 FTS5 cannot be built on it. Move to rusqlite with incremental upserts inside transactions (WAL, busy timeout), keep the daily log authoritative and brauser reindex as the full rebuild, and drop the hand-written writer and the whole-history JSON cache. Keep the existing 6.6 tests (hostile title, case-colliding ID, external edit replaced, heavy-use day with no file write, rollup bounds) passing.
acceptance_criteria: index.db is written through rusqlite with per-delivery incremental updates (no full re-derive or full-file rewrite on a normal delivery); a year-scale fixture stays within bounded per-delivery time and has no 64 MiB ceiling; build_sqlite and the whole-history JSON state are removed or reduced to a bounded watermark; brauser reindex reproduces the same tables; all step 6.6 tests and full suites green.
notes:
2026-10-18 review: native views also read and derive the entire JSON event map rather than querying index.db. The replacement must use indexed card/Recent/worklog queries and representative month/year fixtures, and retain automatic catch-up from authoritative log checkpoints (brwr-ee5). Current native writes already use the configuration lock; preserve that protection while adding SQLite transaction/WAL/busy-timeout semantics.
brwr-ee5 adds format-2 per-file length/mtime ingestion checkpoints and a 64 MiB aggregate changed-log read cap (32 MiB/file), returning unavailable history without partial publication when a pass cannot complete. Real SQLite ingestion should resume bounded batches across requests so cache rebuilds larger than one pass can progress; preserve the source-log recovery, durable-ack independence and stale-history regressions. This is the existing scaling task, not a second SQLite implementation.

title: Refresh the artifact card when the host becomes reachable again
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 8); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. title: Make start_run.requested_at's schema match the timestamps the host accepts
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 10); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. protocol/schema.json:1838 bounds StartRunRequest.requested_at only at minLength 1 / maxLength 32 ('The user's local click time with its UTC offset.'), and protocol/README.md calls it an RFC 3339 timestamp. host/src/native.rs:476-483 validates it with crate::capture::parse_event_time (host/src/capture.rs:1427), which accepts only the 20-byte '...Z' or 25-byte '+HH:MM' whole-second forms, so a schema-valid value with fractional seconds (new Date().toISOString(), '2026-10-27T12:22:48.452Z') is refused as invalid_request 'requested_at must be a current RFC 3339 timestamp'. title: Reload the note under its new key when an external adapter change reaches the panel
description: Confirmed on main 6ad6020 by the 2026-10-27 lane C2 cross-PR seam review (finding 5); file:line references re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4. scheduleReload (extension/panel.ts:491-511) runs reloadConfig and then `void notes.retry()` (panel.ts:507). So when an adapter matching the open page is added or removed elsewhere (the settings page, or Capture Site in another window's panel), watchPolicy fires scheduleReload, the artifact card switches to 'Artifact recognized', but the editor keeps the stale URL key and revision. The user's next autosave sends expected_key kind url; host save_note answers note_conflict reason key_changed (host/src/native.rs:1510) and the typed text moves to the copy-out box. DESIGN.md §6.2 accepts key_changed for an edit already in flight; this is about the next edit after the panel was told.

description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). loadRecent and loadWorklog (extension/panel.ts:605 and :632) return immediately while !session.connected, and the startup IIFE (panel.ts ~815-840: hello, reloadConfig, refreshActiveTab, replayVisits) never reloads them. title: Canonicalize event_id in captured payloads so rescans keep them
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). An activity or why event whose event_id is a valid UUID but not lowercase hyphenated (for example uppercase, or no hyphens) is accepted: CaptureStore::record_activity (host/src/capture.rs:244) returns CaptureOutcome::Persisted. record_entry (capture.rs:770, parse_event_id at :791, hashed at :910) and prepare_batch_entry (capture.rs:604, :622, :667) hash parse_event_id()'s canonical form (capture.rs:1398) into the marker's id_hash, but the hex payload is built from the raw event (record_activity payload clone ~:284, prepare_batch_activity :684-760, record_why :342-378 via serde_json::to_value(event)). On rescan, parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1366) requires sha256(event.event_id) == id_hash (index.rs:1403 activity, :1422 why), so the line is silently dropped and the artifact disappears from the index. Repro: in host/src/index.rs tests, open a CaptureStore with CaptureStore::open_in(&storage(root), None, state) and policy enabled for https://example.com, build activity(...) with occurred_at = now (seconds precision) and event_id = Uuid::new_v4().to_string().to_uppercase(), assert record_activity returns Persisted, then Index::reindex() and assert index.artifact(&event.artifact_id) is Some. It is None on 1c32114. Suggested fix: write the canonical id into the payload at capture (for example insert "event_id" into the marker object next to where record_entry/prepare_batch_entry already insert the normalized "url", capture.rs:653 and :838), covering single activity, batch activity, and why. Optionally also recover lines already written with a raw id by comparing against the canonicalized payload id on rescan. Update 2026-10-27 (lane C2 seam review, findings 18 and 25, re-checked on origin/main 0ab41f4): still reproduces, also for unhyphenated uppercase ids. record_summary already does the right thing: it canonicalizes with parse_event_id before building the marker (host/src/capture.rs:408-415, comment at :408-411) and its test a_noncanonical_uuid_summary_hashes_and_serializes_the_same_spelling (capture.rs:2849-2884) pins it. Copy that approach to the other writers, whose payload still keeps the raw spelling: record_activity (payload = event.clone() at capture.rs:296, serialized at :337), record_why (serde_json::to_value(event) at :373), and batch activity prepare_batch_activity (payload clone at :730, serialized at :764); record_entry (:782, parse_event_id at :803) and prepare_batch_entry (:616, :634) hash the canonical form. The index check is parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1531) at :1568 (activity) and :1587 (why). Mirror the summary test with event_id = canonical.to_uppercase().replace('-', "") for activity and why, then reindex and assert the artifact keeps its focused_seconds and why.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test captures an activity event with an uppercase UUID event_id, asserts Persisted, reindexes, and asserts the artifact is present; a second case covers a why event (single or batch path); each case also uses the unhyphenated uppercase spelling, mirroring a_noncanonical_uuid_summary_hashes_and_serializes_the_same_spelling, and asserts the payload event_id equals the canonical form. Rescans keep lowercase-id events unchanged and still reject a payload whose id does not match the marker hash. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe on local branch probe/lanec-idxw (probe_i5a_uppercase_event_id_survives_a_rescan). P3: real browsers send crypto.randomUUID() lowercase ids, so only a non-standard client hits it. Lane C2 probes: index::tests::probe_v18_noncanonical_event_id_survives_reindex (rb-c2-v18) and index::tests::probe_noncanonical_activity_and_why_ids_survive_reindex (rb-c2-v25); lowercase controls pass.
close_reason: Canonical activity/Why payload and live-index UUIDs preserve rebuilt work; batch replies echo request IDs. Test-first regressions and full gate green on base 46b46495; cycle commit pending driver. Historical recovery tracked by brwr-smu.

title: Bound captured URLs after normalization so rescans keep them
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). Capture checks the raw URL length (event.url.len() > MAX_URL_BYTES at host/src/capture.rs:627 and :802; mode and trail URLs in activity_shape_is_valid at capture.rs:154 and :166) but then stores normalize_url()'s output (capture.rs:1469; page URL inserted at :653/:838, mode URLs at :295/:727, trail from_url ~:313). Percent-encoding can triple the length, so a URL under 8192 bytes raw can be over 8192 normalized. The line is persisted, but on rescan parse_marker_event (host/src/index.rs:1366) applies safe_page_url (index.rs:1483, value.len() <= 8192) to the stored URL at :1396-1402 and drops the event. Repro: in host/src/index.rs tests, capture through CaptureStore::record_activity with event.url = format!("https://example.com/{}", "\u{fc}".repeat(3000)) (6 KB raw, about 18 KB encoded), modes cleared, occurred_at = now; assert Persisted, then Index::reindex() and assert index.artifact(&event.artifact_id) is Some. It is None on 1c32114. Fix: apply the 8192-byte bound after normalization for the page, mode, and trail URLs in every capture path (single, batch, why), rejecting with url_too_long, so nothing is acknowledged that the index will later refuse.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test shows a URL under 8192 bytes raw but over 8192 after normalization is rejected at capture with reason url_too_long (page URL, plus at least one mode or trail URL case), rather than persisted and later dropped; a URL whose normalized form fits is still persisted and survives reindex. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.
notes: Probe on local branch probe/lanec-idxw (probe_i5b_url_that_grows_past_8kib_when_normalized_survives_a_rescan).
close_reason: Reject normalized page/mode/trail URLs above 8192 bytes before vault writes; boundary URLs survive reindex. Test-first regressions and full gate green on base 46b46495; cycle commit pending driver.

title: Offer only View for older notes when the artifact note already exists
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). load_keyed_note (host/src/note.rs:108, ~114-140) returns older_notes whether or not the artifact note exists; NoteEditor passes them straight to showOlderNotes (extension/note-editor.ts ~186), and renderOlderNotes (extension/panel.ts:222-246) always adds a "Use as artifact note" button. use_as_artifact_note (note.rs ~597-601) always refuses when the artifact note exists ("an artifact note already exists; the older note was left unchanged"), so the offered action can only fail. Repro: in extension/tests/panel.test.mjs, answer load_note with exists: true, key {kind: artifact}, body "shared" and one older_notes entry; after the body loads, assert no element in older-note-list has data-older-action="use". One is rendered on 1c32114. Fix: pass the exists flag (or equivalent) to the older-note view and render only View when the artifact note exists; keep Use when it does not.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test shows that with an existing artifact note each older note offers View but not Use, and with no artifact note it offers both; read-only viewing still works. typecheck, lint, build:extension and test:extension green. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix.
notes: Probe on local branch probe/lanec-panel (extension/tests/panel-probes.test.mjs, P5 probe).
close_reason: Offer View only when the shared artifact note exists; availability updates after saves and conflicts. Five new regression scenarios and the full local gate pass; driver commit SHA pending.

title: Keep the older note's URL when migrating it to the artifact note
description: Confirmed on main 1c32114 (2026-10-27 lane C review). use_as_artifact_note (host/src/note.rs:586-636) renders the migrated note with render_note(artifact_key, destination_url, ...) at note.rs:622, so the artifact note records the route the migration was clicked from. save_keyed_note (note.rs:156, effective_canonical_url at ~216-227) keeps an artifact-keyed note's original URL instead. Repro: in host/src/note.rs tests, save_note(&vault, "https://example.com/board?selected=7", ...) to create a URL note, then use_as_artifact_note(&vault, "https://example.com/items/7", &RecordKey{kind: Artifact, value: "work:example.com/7"}, source_url, &revision); read it back with vault.read_note(&key, current_url) and assert artifact_keyed_note_url(&raw, &key) (note.rs:481) equals the source URL. On 1c32114 it is the destination URL. Fix: render with the older note's recorded URL. Sequencing: PR #70 (fix/note-context-identity, note identity from recorded adapter contracts) changes which older-note candidates are offered; do this only after #70 is on main, and re-check the line numbers then.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test migrates a URL-keyed note from route A to an artifact note opened on route B and asserts the artifact note's recorded URL is A, matching save_keyed_note's policy; later saves keep it. The regression test must be added first and shown to fail on main before the fix; full Rust and extension suites green.

title: Explain why the current page is outside capture
description: The new page-pattern review shows what shapes a site has, while the artifact card still says only that an unmatched page is not an artifact. Give a person an actionable explanation on a configured site: capture paused, site removal pending, tenant outside scope, or no matching page rule. Use the same compiled policy and avoid guessing from link patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Panel shows an accurate plain-language reason for a capture miss, links to the existing appropriate settings/review action, distinguishes paused and out-of-scope states, and never treats a link count as visit evidence or widens capture. Cover composed panel states and policy changes.
close_reason: Panel explains capture exclusions using revision-cached policy with settings/review actions; 14 new composed-panel cases and the full gate pass. Cycle 13 diff is based on 71bbbba1; driver records the cycle commit.

title: Curate a worklog before copying it
description: Recent and the native worklog make captured work visible, but copying a day or week currently includes every recorded artifact. Let a person prepare a concise update by selecting the artifact-day rows they want to share and previewing the result, without altering measured activity or creating an AI dependency.
acceptance_criteria: After the ordered plan gates, add explicit row selection and a plain-text preview that preserves validated titles, links, measured totals and chosen period for selected work only. Poll refresh retains selected stable identities, omitted/private work stays out of Copy, and the clipboard receives exactly the preview. No source log/note edits or external credentials.

title: Inject a disposable config path into scripted host lifecycle tests
description: Restoring Windows CI exposed that the killing_the_host_closes_its_open_dialog integration fixture isolates ConfigStore::load through HOME. Windows Known Folders do not use that override, so the host could read the real per-user configuration. The host-level fixture stays Unix-only while the direct scripted child lifecycle tests run on both platforms.
acceptance_criteria: A debug scripted-dialogs-only configuration-path seam confines host lifecycle tests to their temporary directory on Windows and Unix; the host-kill test runs on both without reading user configuration, showing UI or enabling the seam in release builds. Existing macOS smoke config expectations stay valid.
close_reason: Implemented debug scripted-only absolute config override, isolated both host picker fixtures and cache, and verified four process-boundary regressions plus the full gate. Cycle 13 diff is based on 71bbbba1; driver records the cycle commit.

title: Show ambiguous historical notes for explicit read-only viewing
description: When several artifacts share a canonical URL after capture rules are removed, Brauser correctly falls back to the URL key and refuses stale artifact saves. The person still needs a way to find and read those preserved artifact notes without restoring capture or inspecting files manually. Add a small panel disclosure listing verified historical note titles and identities.
acceptance_criteria: The panel lists bounded host-verified candidate notes when historical identity is ambiguous; an explicit choice opens one read-only without changing the primary autosave key, migrating files, or enabling capture. Cover occupied URL notes, multiple candidates, unavailable history, unowned files and response bounds with native and panel tests.
close_reason: Added explicit bounded preserved-note discovery and a separate read-only copyable viewer; native ownership/address rechecks preserve URL autosave identity and capture. Full gate green: 955 Rust outcomes (43 IPC skips), 15 extension files, 144 individually exercised panel cases. Commit: feat: browse preserved artifact notes without changing autosave (driver assigns SHA).

title: Preserve single-event recovery across presentation changes
description: Discovered while reviewing brwr-1fo: VisitIntent v1 stores only the hash of the rendered entry. After an upgrade changes escaping or Unicode filtering, a legacy single-event intent whose marker was not completed compares the new rendered bytes with the old hash and returns retryable/manual repair. Complete markers still deduplicate; compact batch intents retain their exact prepared bytes. This is fail-closed and preserves the log, but the queued legacy visit cannot finish automatically. Give single-event recovery a bounded representation independent of future renderer revisions, with an explicit safe recovery path for older intents; never guess at or overwrite an edited log.
acceptance_criteria: A regression starts with pre-upgrade legacy intent/hash and torn bytes, then retries under a changed renderer without losing the event, duplicating a complete marker, or changing unrelated log bytes. Altered logs, changed selected roots and mismatched payloads remain refused. Cover legacy records drained through both single and batch delivery. Keep any persisted prepared bytes bounded and host-owned.
notes: Completed v2 prepared-byte journals with 512 KiB entry/1 MiB serialized caps and frozen renderer-independent payload identity. V1 recovery retained explicitly. Four new regressions, 52 capture tests and full required/README gate green: 923 Rust outcomes including 43 explicit IPC skips, all 15 extension and two script files, 10,696 inert renderings. Complete diff reviewed locally; no live API or macOS smoke. Driver commit pending, based on ba8ee6b3; .bosun_commit_msg prepared.
close_reason: Retain bounded prepared bytes and normalized payload identity for single-event recovery through single and batch delivery; acceptance and full gate green. Cycle commit pending driver, based on ba8ee6b3; message in .bosun_commit_msg.

title: Show the incoming trail on the artifact card
description: The host already records cross-tool trail edges, but the current artifact card exposes only a linked count. A person returning to a ticket cannot see which pull request or document brought them there. After the ordered plan work, show bounded, host-derived incoming provenance in the card, as anticipated by DESIGN.md section 5.7. This was noticed while restricting transition kinds in brwr-rto; use validated known trails and never infer an edge from a title or revive unknown legacy transition kinds.
acceptance_criteria: The card shows a bounded list of known incoming source artifacts with title, measured navigation wording and safe explicit links; no-source/back-forward and unresolved cases remain honest. Native-query tests cover validated edge types, limits and unknown legacy values, and composed panel tests cover opening a source using local fixtures. No new origin grant, agent call, inferred relationship, or live-service dependency.
notes: Implemented bounded host-derived incoming source/transition pairs, safe explicit HTTP(S) links, measured navigation labels and recorded days. Protocol v8 adds the required list; logs/cache unchanged. Four new Rust and two panel regressions pass, including unknown legacy transitions and local source activation. Full required/README gate green: 944 Rust outcomes (901 exercised, 43 explicit IPC skips), 1,680 directly exercised extension cases, two script files and 10,696 inert renderings. Full diff reviewed locally; no live API review or macOS smoke on Linux. Driver commit pending; excluded .bosun_commit_msg prepared.

description: DESIGN.md is 190 KB of long paragraphs mixing spec, as-built notes and probe transcripts, read every cycle; apply_patch has failed against it. Move dated as-built and probe records to docs/history.md, keep DESIGN.md as the current contract with links, and make AGENTS.md 'Current state' a short table.

description: adapter_id_history only shrinks when an exact contract is restored, inside a 64 KiB config cap. When it fills, unrelated writes (pause, add a site) fail with a generic size error. Add a budget, a distinct error, and a safe prune path (or fold it into the re-key migration). From the 2026-10-16 architecture review.

Four new Rust regressions cover unrelated writes, refused growth/preflight, identity preservation, legacy total-file pressure and native replies. Complete diff reviewed; full required and README gate green: 940 Rust outcomes (897 exercised, 43 explicit IPC skips), all 15 extension and 2 script files, and 10,696 inert Markdown renderings. No live API review or macOS smoke on Linux. Driver commit pending; .bosun_commit_msg prepared.

title: Use one adapter identity for consent and transition checks
description: consent.rs (approval identity) and config.rs (adapter contracts, frozen-ID transitions) compute adapter identity separately, so the confirmation text can drift from what is enforced. Share one identity function. From the 2026-10-16 architecture review.
acceptance_criteria: Both call one identity function; existing consent and transition tests pass unchanged; full suites green.
close_reason: Obsolete: protocol v6 removed the native consent identity (open access PR 1, brwr-oa1).

title: Share one authorize-and-open path across the delivery entry points
description: record_visit, record_activity and record_batch (native.rs) each repeat lock, refresh, policy checks and CaptureStore/CapturePolicy setup, and capture.rs has near-identical mode/trail authorization loops and two persistence pipelines. Extract the shared steps and set a release to remove the legacy entry points. From the 2026-10-16 architecture review.
acceptance_criteria: One shared helper; legacy paths delegate to it; no behavior change; full suites green.

title: Share panel list or run-card text rendering when a second consumer needs it
description: Recent, the worklog and the artifact card shipped without a shared helper, and DESIGN §12.2 step 6.7 is done, so there is no longer a before-6.7 prerequisite. Open access agent runs (spec 2026-10-26 §5.3) are polled through get_run with since_offset, not streamed over a host protocol, so any text helper is an incremental append of polled run-card text, not a streaming renderer. Extract a small framework-free keyed-list or append-only text helper only when Capture Site or the open access run card (PR 3) repeats rendering logic that already exists in the panel; do not rewrite shipped views solely to create an abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: A pure, unit-tested helper is extracted from a concrete repeated need and used by both the existing view and the new consumer (Capture Site or the polled run card); untrusted text stays text-only, never HTML; typecheck, lint and extension tests green. If no second consumer appears by the time open access PR 3 ships, close this item as not needed.
notes: 2026-10-27: reworded. Step 6.7 shipped and open access runs are polled (get_run), so the before-6.7 and streaming framing were obsolete. Kept P3 as a wait-for-a-consumer item.

title: Deliver overflow evidence after the final batch drains
description: Step 6.5 preserves overflow that occurs while an in-flight batch is awaiting acknowledgement, but if that terminal batch empties the queue the remaining overflow marker waits for a future captured event because record_batch requires an authorized event anchor. Make the evidence independently deliverable without inventing an unvalidated vault path or URL.
acceptance_criteria: A regression drops activity while the final batch is in flight, acknowledges that batch, captures no later event, and proves the remaining count and time range are durably marked exactly once; the host still derives every log target from validated data.
close_reason: Standalone overflow batches now drain after the final event, with durable frozen snapshots, bounded retries and host-derived log targets. Three worker cases and four Rust regressions pass; the full required gate is green (936 Rust outcomes including existing sandbox IPC skips, 15 extension files, 2 script files and 10,696 inert renderings). Cycle commit prepared in .bosun_commit_msg; the driver assigns the final SHA.

title: Group cross-tool work into named focus sessions
description: Recent and the worklog explain which artifacts were active, but they cannot express why a Jira issue, design document, and pull request belonged to the same deliberate block of work. Add an explicit local focus session a user can start/name/end from the panel; associate measured activity with its stable session identity and surface the grouped trail in the worklog without inferring intent or contacting a service.
acceptance_criteria: DESIGN.md defines session ownership, privacy, restart, overlap, and append-only log contracts; the panel can start, display, rename, and end one active session; worker restart preserves it; activity and the derived worklog group exact artifacts under it; tests cover hour boundaries, restart, pause, rename, and an artifact active across two sessions; the full suite is green.

title: Offer non-destructive adapter document repair
description: The brwr-rhg recovery path deliberately removes the whole invalid adapter document. Give users a copy-out and whole-document replacement workspace so a malformed entry can be repaired without discarding otherwise useful rules, while never interpreting or auto-migrating an unsupported future format.
acceptance_criteria: When adapter_issue is present, settings can copy the preserved raw document and submit a complete format-1 replacement through TypeScript preview, revision checking, native authorization, and host validation; stale revisions and still-invalid replacements are refused; reset-all remains available; focused tests cover unsupported formats and malformed artifacts.

title: Make first-tool setup one coherent transaction
description: Cookie's own proposal, only after the plan work. Let a new user choose Jira, SharePoint/OneDrive or GitHub first, enter the exact tenant and any required scope, then request Chrome access and native-confirm the site plus starter together. Roll back a newly acquired grant on cancel; retain it when notes or another site purpose already needs it.
acceptance_criteria: A new user can pick a tool, scope it, and confirm site plus starter in one native confirmation; cancel rolls back a newly acquired Chrome grant; tests cover rollback and retained-grant cases.
notes: When composing first-tool setup, show installed GitHub PR and issue owner scopes separately; do not infer one shared editable scope when their policies differ.
close_reason: Superseded by open access (spec 2026-10-26): there is no Chrome grant to request or roll back and no native confirmation; the choose-and-scope part is folded into brwr-1hj Capture Site.
